title: `str.find`: a 0-based byte offset, NULL when absent
verdict: byte offset from 0; NULL where `strpos` is 0
description: `str.find(t)` returns the byte offset of the first match, from 0, or NULL when there is none: `find('héllo', 'l')` is 3 (the character position is 2), and `find('', 'a')` is NULL. The empty pattern is found at 0.
No upstream test pins byte offsets on non-ASCII text; it may change between versions.
reference: `strpos(s, t)` is the 1-based character position of the first match, 0 when there is none (#209). A writer adds 1 and maps NULL to 0, and on text that is not ASCII it needs the character position (the bytes before the match are not the characters).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

notes: Streaming gives what in memory gives on every probe and observation cited here.

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each probe one row at a time and on a 6000-row column with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')`, and each observation twice: its `df(...)` frame's `select`, `with_columns`, `filter`, `sort`, `unique`, `join` and `group_by` go through the streaming engine the second time (`StreamingFrame`); the `s-` observations collect a lazy query on each engine themselves. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.

evidence.note: 'Return the bytes offset of the first substring matching a pattern'; None when not found
test_str_find: 0-based offsets and None on no match, ASCII only (in-memory); bytes vs characters not pinned
